:::

:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Which layer to use for integration if .X is not to be used. Should match the layer of the --reference dataset.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--input_obs_batch_label`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The .obs field in the input (query) dataset containing the batch labels.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string` [required]{.arg-required}

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"sample"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--input_obs_size_factor`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Key in adata.obs for size factor information. Instead of using library size as a size factor,
the provided size factor column will be used as offset in the mean of the likelihood.
Assumed to be on linear scale.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--input_obs_categorical_covariate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys in adata.obs that correspond to categorical data. These covariates can be added in
addition to the batch covariate and are also treated as nuisance factors
(i.e., the model tries to minimize their effects on the latent space).
Thus, these should not be used for biologically-relevant factors that you do _not_ want to correct for.
Important: the order of the categorical covariates matters and should match the order of the covariates in the reference data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--input_obs_continuous_covariate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys in adata.obs that correspond to continuous data. These covariates can be added in
addition to the batch covariate and are also treated as nuisance factors
(i.e., the model tries to minimize their effects on the latent space). Thus, these should not be
used for biologically-relevant factors that you do _not_ want to correct for.
Important: the order of the continuous covariates matters and should match the order of the covariates in the reference data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--input_var_gene_names`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.var column containing gene names. By default, use the index.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--sanitize_ensembl_ids`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to sanitize ensembl ids by removing version numbers.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::::

### scVI, scANVI and scArches training options

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--early_stopping`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to perform early stopping with respect to the validation set.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--early_stopping_monitor`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Metric logged during validation set epoch.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"elbo_validation"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"elbo_validation"`, `"reconstruction_loss_validation"`, `"kl_local_validation"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--early_stopping_patience`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of validation epochs with no improvement after which training will be stopped.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `45`

[Min]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--early_stopping_min_delta`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Minimum change in the monitored quantity to qualify as an improvement, i.e. an absolute change of less than min_delta, will count as no improvement.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.0`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_epochs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of passes through the dataset, defaults to (20000 / number of cells) * 400 or 400; whichever is smallest.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--reduce_lr_on_plateau`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to monitor validation loss and reduce learning rate when validation set `lr_scheduler_metric` plateaus.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--lr_factor`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Factor to reduce learning rate.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.6`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--lr_patience`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of epochs with no improvement after which learning rate will be reduced.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `30.0`

[Min]{.arg-key} `0.0`
:::
::::
:::::

### Neighbor classifier arguments

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--knn_weights`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Weight function used in prediction. Possible values are:
`uniform` (all points in each neighborhood are weighted equally) or
`distance` (weight points by the inverse of their distance)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"uniform"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"uniform"`, `"distance"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--knn_n_neighbors`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of neighbors to use in k-neighbor graph structure used for fast approximate nearest neighbor search with PyNNDescent.
Larger values will result in more accurate search results at the cost of computation time.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `15`

[Min]{.arg-key} `5`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/annotation/scanvi_scarches/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/workflows/annotation/scanvi_scarches);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/annotation/scanvi_scarches/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
